video_title: Lionel Hollins on wanting to FIGHT EVERYONE in the NBA and how RACIST the NBA was

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on his mindset as a rookie in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: I wanted to prove that I belong.
quotes.quote: I wanted to prove that I belong. I am the sixth pick, I was the first guard taken in the draft. I wanted to prove that I belong. And so, that was the first mindset I had. And then when I got there, and we started training camp, and we had all these veterans. There was only two rookies on the team, and the rest of them were veterans. Most of them didn't want to practice. Most of them didn't even care about winning. There was a lot of strife between the best players, Jeff Petrie and Sidney Wicks, both great players.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on the unprofessional locker room culture of his rookie team
quotes.excerpt: We in the locker room and dude pulls out a cigarette, starts smoking in the locker room.
quotes.quote: We in the locker room and dude pulls out a cigarette, starts smoking in the locker room. And then somebody said, 'Man, let me get a light from your smokes.' Anybody, 'Yo, you got a smoke over there for me?' We got three or four guys smoking in the locker room. And I am like, 'This is the NBA.' And then the fighting at practice all the time. And people competed hard because the salaries weren't big, and if you were the last two or three guys and you were Black, and there was two or three white guys that were there, those three Black guys were gone.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on the racial dynamics of his early NBA teams
quotes.excerpt: The first all-Black team, you know what they were called? The New York Niggaboggers.
quotes.quote: They weren't going to have an all-Black team. The first all-Black team, you know what they were called? The New York Niggaboggers. And then you know who changed the whole climate was Red Auerbach because he started five Blacks with the Boston Celtics. He didn't win everybody over because they were winning, it just happened that over time that they did. But, those types of things and I got called the N-word by my own fans. And this is a story I tell it because of the times, I am not telling it because I am proud of it.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on being booed as a rookie starting over a veteran
quotes.excerpt: I used to get booed because everybody I was starting in place of a veteran white guy.
quotes.quote: I used to get booed because everybody I was starting in place of a veteran white guy. And he was a nice guy, he was a good guy, he wasn't me. You know, he didn't bring the juice that could help us win like that, but he was a big part of us winning the championship. And so, one night, man, they are booing me like crazy. I can't make a shot, I done turned the ball over two or three times, right? I am down on myself already. I didn't need their help.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on his defiant reaction to being booed by fans
quotes.excerpt: My moment was I went to center court and I put up the finger and I bowed.
quotes.quote: Remember 1968 Olympics, George Foreman wins the championship in boxing. He win, pull out two little American flags, walk to center ring, put them up over his head and he bowed to every section, right? And everybody went crazy. Well, my moment was I went to center court and I put up the finger and I bowed to every section, right? And then walked to the bench. You know, you know how different that would have been now. I probably would have been suspended four or five games or something like that and the media would have been talking about it for a month.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on the intense, physical nature of NBA practices
quotes.excerpt: Every practice was competitive. We didn't watch film, we didn't walk through, we practiced, we scrimmaged.
quotes.quote: Every practice was competitive. We didn't watch film, we didn't walk through, we practiced, we scrimmaged and we got after it. And you know, you had to not just beat the person you were going against, but you also had to help the team you on win. See, that was more important than just numbers back then. And we had that conversation later on, you and I.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on his relationship with coach Pete Maravich
quotes.excerpt: He was my dog. He was my roadie, and he protected me.
quotes.quote: He was my dog. He was my roadie, and he protected me. We were playing in New Orleans in the Superdome, and Pete Maravich elbowed me and I hit him upside the head. All of a sudden this 6-11 backup center come off the bench at me, chasing me, right? Lou intercepted him. Fight's over, right? And so, he said, 'Boy, do you know we down here in Louisiana? You can get, huh, hitting Pete Maravich like that?' Because you know Pete was a star, he was the guy. And so, I didn't know. All I knew is that he, he was trying to hurt me.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on the lack of 'bluffing' in NBA fights
quotes.excerpt: Nobody bluffed back then. When they were fighting, when they were mad, they fought.
quotes.quote: And that was the difference between then. You know all this hard fouling and knocking people out there, you do that, somebody is raising, they are coming at you from the ground up. They are not waiting for somebody to grab you and point fingers, they come like you. I don't bluff. Nobody bluffed back then. When they were fighting, when they were mad, they fought. And there was some big-time fights. So, that was the times of there.

quotes.speaker: Lionel Hollins
quotes.summary_phrase: Lionel Hollins on the toughness of non-star players in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: There was a lot of tough guys and you didn't have to be a star to be tough.
quotes.quote: There was a lot of tough guys and you didn't have to be a star to be tough. They were just toughness because they were men, they were scrapping trying to take care of their families and trying to stay in that league, you know. And now, you get a lifetime contract when you get drafted. Forget coming in and earning it. But, you know, I would have liked some of the medical things and the less harsh practices.
